content: 1. The Health Adaptation Planning document was accessed on July 26, 2015. 2. This document, contributed by Working Group I, was accessed on July 26, 2015. 3. This was a contribution by Working Group II to the Fifth Assessment Report, published by Cambridge University Press in 2014. 4. This research, published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2012, emphasizes the use of adaptive management to enhance resilience and adaptive capacity. 7. 8. The Vision 2030 report, which focuses on the resilience of water supply and sanitation systems in the context of climate change, was accessed on July 26, 2015. 11. A meeting report on the consultation regarding the Health Emergency Risk Management Framework and public health preparedness, held from November 21–23, 2012, was accessed on August 24, 2015. 13. A document on climate finance was reviewed on July 26, 2015. 14. The WHO website provided information on financial resources for implementing climate change adaptation strategies, accessed on July 26, 2015. 15. A terminology guide on disaster risk reduction was accessed on July 26, 2015. 16. The WHO framework titled Everybody’s Business: Strengthening Health Systems to Improve Health Outcomes was reviewed on July 26, 2015. This document outlines the operational framework for building climate-resilient health systems. It provides guidance for public health professionals, health managers, and decision-makers in related sectors such as nutrition, water, sanitation, and emergency management. It also serves as a resource for international development agencies to focus investments and support for public health, health system strengthening, and climate change adaptation. 17. The framework aims to enhance the capacity of health systems and public health programs to protect health in the face of climate variability and change. By implementing the ten key components outlined in the framework, health organizations and authorities can better anticipate, prevent, prepare for, and manage climate-related health risks. 18. The framework is particularly useful for least-developed countries and those developing the health components of National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). It supports the design of comprehensive responses to risks associated with both short-term climate variability and long-term climate change.
